title: Website care plans

seo.title: Website care plans and maintenance
seo.description: Month-to-month website care: patching, nightly backups with a tested restore, monitoring, four-hour critical response and development hours.

answerBlock: A website care plan is a monthly service that keeps a site secure, backed up, monitored and improving after launch. Calwebtech care plans cover patching, nightly encrypted backups with a quarterly restore drill, monitoring, a four-hour response on anything critical and a fixed allowance of development hours. Plans start at $1,500 a month and run month to month, with no lock-in.

hero.outcome: A site that stays patched, backed up and fast, with someone accountable when it breaks and hours in hand for the next improvement.

problem.heading: When does a website need a care plan?
problem.intro: Care plan enquiries usually follow a scare, a departure or a slow decline.

situations.title: Nobody has owned the site since launch
situations.body: The agency or developer who built it has moved on, updates are months behind and nobody is sure the backups work.

situations.title: Something broke and took days to fix
situations.body: A plugin update, an expired certificate or a hosting problem took the site or its forms down, and enquiries were lost before anyone noticed.

situations.title: Small improvements never happen
situations.body: The list of changes keeps growing, because each one needs a quote, a purchase order and a wait.

included.heading: What is included in a website care plan?
included.intro: Every plan includes the essentials below. The development allowance and response times are written into the plan.
items: Security patching and updates, tested on staging before production
A quarterly restore drill, so the backup is proven, not promised
Uptime, certificate and form monitoring, with alerts to our team
A four-hour response on anything critical
A fixed allowance of development hours each month for improvements
A quarterly funnel review of enquiries, speed and search health
Performance and accessibility checks against the site's budget
Month-to-month terms, with the code and accounts always in your name

process.heading: How does a website care plan work?
process.intro: Onboarding in the first two weeks, then a steady monthly and quarterly rhythm.

steps.title: Onboarding audit
steps.body: Access, hosting, backups, updates, security and speed reviewed, with anything urgent fixed first and a written list of the rest.

steps.title: Monitoring and patching
steps.body: Updates tested on staging and applied, backups checked, and uptime, certificates and forms watched continuously.

steps.title: Development allowance
steps.body: Improvements from your list, prioritised with you and delivered from the fixed allowance of hours.

steps.title: Restore drill and review
steps.body: A backup restored to prove it works, and a funnel review of enquiries, speed and search health with agreed next steps.

technology.heading: Which platforms do your care plans cover?
technology.intro: Sites we built and sites we did not, once the onboarding audit shows they can be looked after safely.

pricing.heading: How much does a website care plan cost?
pricing.intro: Plans start at $1,500 a month, month to month. The price follows the size of the development allowance and how much the site depends on integrations.

factors.title: Development allowance
factors.body: More monthly hours for improvements is the main thing that moves the price.

factors.title: Platform and complexity
factors.body: A marketing site is simpler to look after than a store or web application with integrations and background jobs.

factors.title: Hosting
factors.body: A plan can include managing hosting on infrastructure in your name, or work with the host you already use.

factors.title: The site's starting point
factors.body: A site that is months behind on updates needs a one-off catch-up before the monthly plan starts.

faq.heading: What do buyers ask about website care plans?

items.question: Do you look after websites you did not build?
items.answer: Yes, once the onboarding audit shows the site can be looked after safely. If it cannot, we tell you what needs fixing first and quote that separately.

items.question: What counts as a critical issue?
items.answer: Anything that takes the site or its forms down, exposes data, or stops orders or enquiries. Those get a four-hour response. Everything else is handled in the normal monthly rhythm.

items.question: Is there a minimum term?
items.answer: No. Care plans are month to month. If we stop being useful you should be able to leave, and take the code with you.

items.question: What happens to development hours we do not use?
items.answer: The plan sets out how many hours you get each month and what happens to any left over, in writing, before you start. We keep a prioritised list of improvements ready so the hours are easy to use.

items.question: How do you know the backups work?
items.answer: We restore one every quarter. A backup that has never been restored is a hope rather than a backup, so the drill is part of every plan.

items.question: Can our team still make changes while we are on a plan?
items.answer: Yes. Your team keeps full access and publishes content as normal. We ask that code changes go through staging, so updates and backups stay reliable.

items.question: Can we move the site elsewhere later?
items.answer: Yes. The code, database and accounts stay in your name throughout, so leaving needs a handover call rather than a negotiation.

enquiry.heading: How do I get a care plan quote?
enquiry.intro: Send the address of your site and what worries you about it today. We reply within one business day, and the quote follows a short look at the site.
enquiry.footnote: Protected by bot filtering. We never sell or share your details, and you can ask us to delete them at any time.

success.heading: Thanks. Your request is with us.
success.body: We will look at your site and reply by email within one business day.
